_comment: [F60 §3] WARM-RUNNER BINARY PINS. Every byte the F60 warm VM installs is pinned here BEFORE it is installed: scripts/f60-bootstrap.ps1 dot-sources the SHIPPED F59 verifier (payloads/f59-prebuilt-verify.ps1 -> Test-F59AssetSha256) and REFUSES an empty pin, a malformed pin or a digest mismatch. There is no warn-and-continue path and no 'download whatever is latest' URL anywhere in the F60 lane (main.yml's Tailscale step still fetches tailscale-setup-latest-amd64.msi - that file is NOT touched by F60; the warm VM pins an explicit version instead).

tailscale_msi.name: tailscale-setup-1.102.5-amd64.msi
tailscale_msi.source_kind: official Tailscale package host (pkgs.tailscale.com/stable). The version is EXPLICIT - the '-latest-' URL main.yml uses is banned on the warm VM because a moving URL cannot be pinned.
tailscale_msi.bootstrap_note: Digest is recorded by .github/workflows/f60-warm-pins-bootstrap.yml (one click, GitHub-hosted) and committed here. This sandbox could not reach pkgs.tailscale.com to compute it, and an invented digest would be worse than an empty one: an empty pin is REFUSED at install time.

nssm.name: nssm-2.24.zip
nssm.source_kind: official NSSM release zip (nssm.cc/release). win64/nssm.exe is extracted from it and staged to C:\ghrdp\tools\nssm.exe.
nssm.bootstrap_note: Same one-click digest bootstrap as tailscale_msi (nssm.cc is not reachable from the agent sandbox).

node_win_x64_zip.source_kind: official Node.js distribution (nodejs.org/dist). The bootstrap workflow resolves the newest LTS release of the pinned major (20), downloads node-v<ver>-win-x64.zip, and CROSS-CHECKS the computed digest against the published SHASUMS256.txt line before recording it - two independent sources must agree.
node_win_x64_zip.bootstrap_note: version/name/url/sha256 are all filled by the bootstrap run (nodejs.org is not reachable from the agent sandbox). Node is needed on the warm VM for scripts/serve-dist.mjs (the ghrdp-ui-nssm service) and for scripts/f59-verify-sha256.mjs (the fail-closed bundle verifier).

actions_runner_win_x64_zip.name: actions-runner-win-x64-2.337.0.zip
actions_runner_win_x64_zip.source_kind: official actions/runner GitHub release. The digest is the value published in the release notes' 'SHA-256 Checksums' section for win-x64 (read through the GitHub API on 2026-10-01); f60-warm-pins-bootstrap.yml RE-ASSERTS it against the release notes of the pinned tag before the warm VM ever downloads it.

reused_f59_assets._comment: The transport binaries and the dashboard bundle are NOT re-pinned here: they come from the F59 releases with the F59 pins, so the warm VM and the GitHub-hosted lane can never drift apart.

repo_access_note: dekarita/supreme-lamp is a PRIVATE repository, so the warm VM cannot fetch the repo's own release assets anonymously and it has no GITHUB_TOKEN outside a job. The bootstrap therefore takes an OPTIONAL RepoAccessToken parameter (repo secret GHRDP_RELEASE_READONLY_TOKEN: a fine-grained PAT, Contents read-only, this repository only, short expiry). It is used ONLY for release-asset downloads, is masked in the provisioning log, is never written to any VM log, and is deleted from the Run Command runtime-settings files when the bootstrap finishes. Without it the three release assets are skipped with a LOUD label (warm-stage=deferred-to-dispatch) and warm-dispatch.yml stages them per run with the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN.
fail_closed: scripts/f60-bootstrap.ps1 refuses to install anything whose pin is empty or mismatched (it reuses Test-F59AssetSha256, which throws on both). .github/workflows/provision-warm-runner.yml additionally fails at preflight when the pins file is missing, when a pin is not 64-hex, or when payloads/f59-prebuilt-pins.json is absent - before it ever logs in to Azure.
